description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related measures (Final Acc, Δ Acc, and Initial Acc) vary as a function of “Initial Confidence.” The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0.95 to 0.99 with tick marks at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, and 0.99 (interval 0.01). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 up to 1.0 with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 (interval 0.2). The “Final Acc” series is shown as a solid blue line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it is about 0.90 at 0.95, decreases to about 0.86 at 0.96, rises to about 0.89 at 0.97 and about 0.93 at 0.98, then ends around 0.88 at 0.99 (with the largest error bar at 0.99). The “Δ Acc” series is shown as an orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it is about 0.90 at 0.95, about 0.86 at 0.96, about 0.88 at 0.97, about 0.87 at 0.98, and drops to about 0.75 at 0.99 (also with a noticeably larger error bar at 0.99 than at earlier x-values). The “Initial Acc” series is shown as a green dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it is near 0.00 at 0.95 and 0.96, around 0.01 at 0.97, around 0.05 at 0.98, and increases to about 0.13 at 0.99, where its error bar is much larger than at the preceding points.
